design.affected_system: rights-preserving compliance assistance, incentives, inspections, and enforcement
alternatives: screen feasible locations against the largest access gaps for compliance assistance and technical-support locations
co-optimize distributed and high-capacity locations for compliance assistance and technical-support locations
pair access, privacy, language, neutrality, skill, and capacity-aware siting with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Eligibility, notice, awareness, capability, action, inspection, violation, sanction, and outcome remain distinct.
No behavioral score automatically triggers enforcement, benefit denial, or coercive action.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: retain only existing approved locations for compliance assistance and technical-support locations.

constraints.description: The compliance, incentives, and behavioral policy site must respect declared land control, accessibility, permitting, safety, and operating feasibility.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: regulatory operations director and behavioral insights lead
design.decision_question: Where should non-enforcement assistance, document, inspection, and technical services reduce verified barriers?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The compliance, incentives, and behavioral policy site must respect declared land control, accessibility, permitting, safety, and operating feasibility.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for compliance assistance and technical-support locations passes documented checks for parcel control, legal authority, environmental review, access, capacity, and operator responsibility.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: access, privacy, language, neutrality, skill, and capacity-aware siting
independence_key.primary_outcome: eligible cases beyond usable qualified assistance

design.intended_claim: A versioned site design for comparing declared alternatives affecting compliance assistance and technical-support locations, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: eligible cases beyond usable qualified assistance
distributional gap in eligible cases beyond usable qualified assistance
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call a candidate assistance site trusted, neutral, accessible, qualified, or used.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for compliance assistance and technical-support locations passes documented checks for parcel control, legal authority, environmental review, access, capacity, and operator responsibility.

design.title: Site compliance assistance and technical-support access
transportability_risks: Law, administrative burden, trust, incentives, capability, enforcement, and baseline behavior differ.
Observed compliance may reflect detection and documentation rather than underlying behavior.

family.affected_system: rights-preserving compliance assistance, incentives, inspections, and enforcement
claim_boundary: Area and administrative differences do not establish discrimination, preferences, or individual behavior.
Behavioral and allocation designs require rights, accessibility, privacy, and non-coercion review.
Causal, fairness, adoption, and welfare claims require direct outcomes and independent governance evidence.
family.decision_owner: regulatory operations director and behavioral insights lead
family.description: Eight decisions for process diagnosis, workload forecasting, policy portfolios, service siting, support allocation, contact scheduling, behavior stress, and incentive evaluation.
family.title: Compliance, incentives, and behavioral policy

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
